To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the HLA B15 antigen is associated with cell mediated immune reactions to pancreatic islet cell antigens and that this antigen is associated with the presence of ICAs in the serum of patients with type 1 diabetes.

(1) the frequency of HIA B8 and B 15 is increased in patients with juvenile onset type diabetes; (2) the incidence of islet cell autoantibodies is high in the early stages of juvenile onset type diabetes and declines with time; (3) the frequency of cell-mediated immune reactions is increased in patients who are HLA B15 positive and who have other tissue autoantigbodies; (4) diabetic siblings have identical HLA A B haplotypes

the HLA antigens of juvenile onset type diabete patients differ from those of maturity onset type diabeties, that islet cell antibodies are found in the majority of patients in the early phase of the disease, but that the presence of these autoantibodies is not correlated to HLA antigens or cell-mediated immune reactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic and environmental aspects of juvenile onset diabetes
the genetic, immunological, and clinical characteristics of juvenile onset diabetics.
the immunogenetic and immunologic aspects of juvenile onset type diabetes mellitus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

HLA B8 is associated with juvenile type diabetics and that the presence of ICAs is associated with the duration of the disease, but that there is no evidence that either HLA type or ICAs have a direct influence on the pathogenesis of the disease.
the HLA system is not a primary cause of diabetes but is involved in the pathogenesis of diabetes in some way.
the HLA system has a major role in the susceptibility to juvenile onset type diabetes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HLA B8 is the most common antigen in juvenile onset type diabetic patients, and that the presence of ICAs decreases with time after the onset of diabetes.
juvenile onset diabetics have an immunological defect, probably genetic in origin, and that this immunological defect can be detected in 32% of juvenile onset patients.
the presence of ICAs in juvenile onset type diabets is not associated with cell-mediated immunity, and that cell-mediated immunity to pancreatic antigens is not associated with HLA type.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HLA system does not play a role in the development of type 2 diabetes.
the HLA B15 antigen was found to be a marker for the presence of cell-mediated immune reactions and other autoantibodies in type 1 diabetes mellitus.
the immune system of juvenile onset type diabetic patients is disturbed, and that the immune disturbance is not related to HLA type or to the presence of ICAs.
